subject: [Whishlist] Ability to export a quantity computed in the "model" part of a Stan model

messages.author: bcfb6bc9f75aae0f
messages.subject: [Whishlist] Ability to export a quantity computed in the "model" part of a Stan model
parts:
I'd like to be able to export quantities used in the computation of the log-posterior without having to re-declare and re-compute them in the "generated quantities" part of a Stan model. After attentive perusal of the Stan manual, I saw no way to do this.

Could it be possible to add, for example, a keyword (e. g. "exported") to the declaration of the quantity ?

Nota Bene : I am aware of the possibility of declaring transformed parameters. But the interesting quantities might be function of other "uninteresting" quantities computed earlier in the model part. Including them in a "transformed parameter" part would export also those "uninteresting" quantities.

Possible applications : DIC, WAIC, mixtures of already-fitted models, etc...

What do you think ?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] [Whishlist] Ability to export a quantity computed in the "model" part of a Stan model
parts:
Other people have asked for this, too.

Basically, the idea is to completely get rid of the transformed
paramters block and instead flag variables declared at the top of
the model block as save or no save.

Right now, the transformed parameters may depend on "uninteresting"
quantities, as in

transformed parameters {
real a;
real b;
{
real c; // uninteresting
real d; // uninteresting

... define a and b ...
}
}

but the uninteresting variables will not be available in the model
block.

The alternative that makes most sense to me would be this:

model {
save real a;
save real b;
real c;
real d;
....
}

- Bob
